mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed in the last week (t-1w to t-0w), indicates a return to office and associated weekday activities, which will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility reverses its recent upward trend or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in PARKS mobility from t-1w to t-0w suggests a shift to less outdoor activity, likely due to changing weather or seasonal patterns, which will negatively impact outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains low but RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and increase in WORKPLACES mobility suggests a shift away from home-based activities towards out-of-home work, which will free up time and opportunity for retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall and WORKPLACES mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The recent uptick in TRANSIT station mobility (t-1w to t-0w), after a period of stagnation, indicates increased commuting and general movement within the city, which typically precedes an increase in RETAIL_REC as people move around more.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility continues to rise but RETAIL_REC declines in the immediate next week, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The relatively stable and slightly positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests that essential errands are being maintained, providing a baseline level of out-of-home activity that prevents RETAIL_REC from falling further and may even support a slight recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines significantly and RETAIL_REC also declines over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low levels of RETAIL_REC, hovering around -30% for three of the last four weeks, indicate a persistent lack of discretionary spending and activity, suggesting it will remain depressed over the next four weeks unless a strong external shock occurs.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below -25% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC breaks above -25% in the next week, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous sharp drop in PARKS mobility and a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests people are neither staying home nor engaging in outdoor leisure, implying a shift towards other out-of-home activities, potentially including retail and recreation, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: If both PARKS and RESIDENTIAL mobility decline, but RETAIL_REC also declines over the next two weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and significant increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggest a policy-driven or widespread return to pre-pandemic routines, which will inevitably boost RETAIL_REC as more people are out and about in commercial areas.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by >10 points week-on-week AND TRANSIT increases by >3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show strong increases, but RETAIL_REC remains stagnant or declines over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.
